subject: Per-endpoint economics: instrumentation & exception playbook
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Per-endpoint economics: instrumentation & exception playbook

Team —

Quick heads-up and ask following a customer conversation with GridScale (Emily Park). They asked for a clear, per-endpoint cost and latency breakdown they can share internally, plus a short "what to do when latency/cost spikes" playbook we can hand them. This came up as part of a renewal conversation and Emily is nervous about sudden cost spikes tied to a few noisy routes.

High-level ask:
- Can Product + Analytics define the minimal set of per-endpoint metrics we need surfaced in Console for customers to attribute spend (tokens, request count, p50/p95 latency, quantization/variant used)?
- Engineering: what’s the fastest, low-risk way to expose a per-endpoint time window (1h/24h/7d) breakdown and a small sample dashboard?
- Ops/Support: draft a simple 1-page playbook for customers describing detection thresholds and recommended fallbacks (route pinning, model variant fallback, cache warm-up).

Attachments: I’ve dropped two stubs (sample CSV + mock dashboard image) and a rough playbook draft in Drive — see links below.

Goal: Have a short customer-ready package (dashboard PNG, 1-page playbook, a HubSpot note) by EOD Friday so Emily has something to share in her internal review.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-04T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Per-endpoint economics: instrumentation & exception playbook

Thanks Vanessa — good call. High-level notes from Product POV: 

- Minimal per-endpoint schema: endpoint_id, route_name, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, requests, success_rate, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, compute_seconds, cost_estimate_usd.
- Time windows: quick toggle for 1h / 24h / 7d is sufficient for first pass.
- UX: show a compact table + sparkline for p95 and cost; allow exporting CSV.

I can own the customer-facing playbook content and HubSpot note. Plan for a lightweight "starter" playbook that includes: detection thresholds, immediate mitigations, longer-term mitigations, and recommended Redwood Console actions.

Next steps: Markus — can you confirm what fields Engineering can produce from existing telemetry in the next 4 business days? Jonas — can Analytics produce a 24h sample for GridScale from last week (anonymized) so Sales has an example?

- Marissa
Product Manager, Console

---

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-04T13:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Per-endpoint economics: instrumentation & exception playbook

We can expose most of that from current request/metrics pipeline but a few caveats:

- compute_seconds and a reliable cost_estimate_usd require joining serving logs with the billing model. We have a prototype join but it’s not surfaced as a single API yet — estimate 6 business days to productionize a safe join and CSV export.
- p95 latency per-route is available; p50 requires minimal additional aggregation.
- model_variant is available in logs for hosted requests; for Dedicated/Private we rely on route metadata which is sometimes missing.

Fast path proposal (low-risk):
1) Export table with fields we can guarantee today: endpoint_id, route_name, model_variant (when present), tokens_in, tokens_out, requests, p50_latency_ms (approx), p95_latency_ms, success_rate. (ETA: 3 business days for a CSV export + sample dashboard PNG)
2) Ship a follow-up CSV that includes a cost_estimate_usd after we finalize the join with billing (ETA +6 business days).

I’ll spin up a quick Grafana dashboard and export a PNG for GridScale. I’ll also attach sample log query we used.

-Markus
Engineering Manager, Serving Platform

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Emily Park <epark@gridscale.ai>
Cc: AWS Marketplace <marketplace@aws.com>
Date: 2027-08-05T16:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Per-endpoint economics: instrumentation & exception playbook

Hi all — attaching anonymized 24h export from last week for a typical mid-sized tenant (see attached CSV). I also exported a basic PNG dashboard that Markus and I iterated on. Quick notes for Emily:

- The CSV contains per-route counts and latencies; cost column is currently a placeholder until the billing join lands.
- We highlighted two noisy routes that accounted for ~62% of variability in spend during a 3-hour window; the playbook recommends pinning to a cheaper model_variant and enabling prefix cache for those routes as immediate mitigations.

Emily — I’ve copied you directly so you can share feedback; if the sample looks useful we can generate a GridScale-specific export once we get consent.

Next steps:
- Marissa: finalize the 1-page playbook PDF (Vanessa needs customer-ready copy by Friday).
- Markus: provide CSV export endpoint and PNG by end of day Thursday (fast path).
- Ops/Sales: Vanessa to confirm internal review cadence with Emily.

Jonas Weber
Data Insights Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced:
- per-endpoint-sample-dashboard.png (attached)
- client-economics-sample.csv (attached)
- playbook-draft-v1.pdf (Drive link)

Forwarded message headers and quoting present in-thread for traceability.
